problem:
The center of the hyperbola $5{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}-20y+4x=-8$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}-20y+4x & =-8 \\ 5{y}^{2}-20y-2{x}^{2}+4x & =-8 \\ 5[{y}^{2}-4y]-2[{x}^{2}-2x] & =-8 \\ 5[(y-2)^{2}-4]-2[(x-1)^{2}-1] & =-8 \\ 5(y-2)^{2}-20-2(x-1)^{2}+2 & =-8 \\ 5(y-2)^{2}-2(x-1)^{2} & =-8+20-2 \\ 5(y-2)^{2}-2(x-1)^{2} & =10 \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{5} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,1,2\,).$
